title: Asia-Pacific Youth Want Real-World Work Skills
paragraphs: Young people in the Asia-Pacific region want more practical, real-world experiences and skills to prepare them for work.
This is what a survey of young people in 10 countries and regions has found. The survey was done by delivery company FedEx and international youth organization Junior Achievement.
It included around 4,200 young people aged 15 to 22 living across Japan, South Korea, China, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.

The survey found that 97% of young people across all these places would like more exposure to how the working world really operates. Also, nine in 10 believe there is a gap between what they are taught and what employers will expect from them.

Ninety percent said understanding how business works on an international scale will matter for their careers. However, close to 30% said their schools or universities haven't taught them how cross-border trade works.
The situation is similar for AI. More than eight in 10 said they think they will need to use it, but only around six in 10 said they are being taught how to do so in a real working environment.
Some are trying to bridge the AI knowledge gap themselves, with 42% saying they are experimenting with it themselves outside of school to learn more.

This may not be surprising, as the survey also revealed a respect for an independent spirit. Eighty-five percent of young people in the Asia-Pacific region agree that having an entrepreneurial mindset can help people succeed in any job.
However, the number of participants who said they were confident in their own entrepreneurial abilities was lower.

Only 61% said they were confident in their ability to come up with new ideas or solutions to problems, while just 59% said they felt they could work independently and make decisions without significant guidance.
